children: , the cloud and enterprise-AI giant, faced a tougher copyright test after news organizations unsealed parts of their summary-judgment filing. Shares slipped approximately 0.8% to $493.84 Friday, reversing part of Thursday's tech-led rebound.

The publishers are zeroing in on testimony from Microsoft and OpenAI executives, arguing that AI-generated answers can reduce the need for readers to visit the original news sites. Microsoft pushed back, saying those comments reflect individual views rather than settling whether its use of copyrighted material qualifies as fair use. That distinction matters: the court has not ruled on the publishers' allegations, leaving the central copyright question very much alive.

For investors, the real pressure point is the economics behind Copilot and AI search. If courts decide that answer engines materially erode publishers' traffic or licensing value, Microsoft could face higher content costs or changes to how its products surface information. The valuation picture adds another wrinkle: at $493.84, Microsoft trades 15.66% below its GF Value estimate of $585.56. That gap suggests the shares already sit well below GuruFocus' estimate of fair value, even as copyright uncertainty hangs over one of Microsoft's biggest AI growth bets.

title: Microsoft Slips as AI Testimony Sharpens Copyright Risk
